entries.title: Bears practice report: Bears K Cairo Santos says he and Packers WR Matthew Golden resolved conflict, moved on
entries.summary: <p>What happened Thursday at Halas Hall:</p><h3><b>Santos moves on</b></h3><h3></h3><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> kicker Cairo Santos copped to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/12/video-bears-k-cairo-santos-packers-wr-matthew-golden-appear-to-exchange-cheap-shots-on-punt-return" >trying to trip Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden </a>on a punt return Sunday and said he and Golden cleared the air on the incident at halftime. Golden knocked down a Bears staffer on the sideline, then Santos stuck his leg out as Golden returned to the field.</p><p>Santos said he saw Golden bump the staff member, but didn’t want to elaborate on the incident. He said he has not heard from the NFL about potential discipline.</p><p>"It's all good," Golden said Sunday. "I ain't got nothing to say to him."</p><h3><b>Chance for Stevenson</b></h3><h3></h3><p>With the Bears reeling from Packers quarterback Jordan Love lighting them up, they need all the help they can get in the secondary. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, who frequently plays through injuries, practiced Thursday despite a hip issue and could be available Sunday against the Falcons.</p><h3><b>Pass rushers wanted</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears haven’t added any pass-rushing help in the wake of defensive end Montez Sweat’s suspension and lineman Dayo Odeyingbo’s quad injury. They could start recently activated lineman Shemar Turner, but defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has warned that any player coming off a long layoff won’t play a full load of snaps.</p><h3><b>Minus Monangai</b></h3><h3></h3><p>It’s looking increasingly likely running back Kyle Monangai (toe) will miss the Falcons game. He hasn’t practiced since getting hurt against the Jets on Oct. 4.</p><h3><b>Other absences</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quad) did not practice, and Edwards is unlikely to play against the Falcons. Veteran defensive tackle Grady Jarrett and left guard Joe Thuney are not injured, but got a rest day.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Once upon a midnight dreary, Prairie State pumpkins grew so cheery, over many a farmer's field in the land we call "downstate."</p><p>Glowing orange and growing larger, soon they're plucked for pies and larders -- or, perhaps, to meet the edge of carving knives shall be their fate!</p><p>Now a "jack-o-lantern" name them, spooking folks throughout our state -- so share your pic, don't hesitate!</p><p><contribly-widget assignment-id="a8bd0318-5117-462d-a6f6-20b613cd0c87" client-id="b20193c8-5c0c-4a5b-a770-64305c544c4e" api-url="https://api.contribly.com/1" locale="en-gb"></contribly-widget></p><script src="https://contribly-widgets.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/multi-part/multi-part.js" async crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

entries.title: Woman, 34, dies in Roseland house fire
entries.summary: <p>A woman died in a fire in Roseland Thursday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The unidentified 34-year-old woman was inside a residence in the 10500 block of South Indiana Avenue at 3 p.m. when it caught fire, police said. </p><p>She was pronounced dead at the scene.</p><p>Detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams bristles at reporting on hamstring injury, but provides little clarity
entries.summary: <p>This was one of the strangest days of Caleb Williams’ time as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback, and that’s saying something given the various absurdities of his rookie season.</p><p>As he continued working back from a hamstring injury with an eye on returning Sunday against the Falcons, Williams spoke publicly Thursday for the first time since getting hurt nearly a month ago. He said he didn’t know whether he’d play in Atlanta, but felt strong, fast and relatively normal after going through a full practice.</p><p>But the focus was predominantly on his annoyance with what he called incorrect reporting about the injury.</p><p>Williams said he suffered “a hamstring tear — and a pretty serious one,” in response to reports that he had a Grade 2 hamstring strain. A Grade 2 strain includes some muscle tearing, but Williams refused multiple requests to specify.</p><p>“If you haven’t heard it from [coach Ben Johnson] or me, it would probably be wrong, which every single one has been,” he said in a four-minute opening statement.</p><p>Williams said the media was “not deserving” of him clarifying the severity of the injury after weeks of what he deemed false reporting. He was unwilling to explain further and repeatedly said, “Next question,” as a Bears staffer interjected to stop the exchange.</p><p>All hamstring strains involve muscle tearing, according to Cleveland Clinic, and the grade is determined by severity. A Grade 1 wouldn’t fit the limited description he gave, while a Grade 3 could require surgery and likely would cost a player months. It’s difficult to grasp the objection without him clarifying.</p><p>If Williams returns relatively soon, whether Sunday, next Thursday against the Patriots or Nov. 2 against the Seahawks, his recovery time would line up with what is typical for a Grade 2 strain.</p><p>All the friction could easily have been corrected or, better yet, avoided.</p><p>The disconnect began the day after Williams went down Sept. 20 against the Vikings when Johnson declined to rule him out for the very next game when asked directly. While that response seemed disingenuous at the time, it fueled backlash toward Williams online and in the national media for what was perceived as overreacting to the injury when he was carted to the locker room in tears.</p><p>Johnson has been asked several times since about Williams’ injury and rehabilitation and responded minimally. Williams also has been at Halas Hall and crossed paths with reporters in the locker room, even saying hello, but never asked for a minute to clear things up.</p><p>That would’ve been reasonable, especially for a player who has had such a cordial relationship with the media. When former Bears quarterback Justin Fields took a shot at the coaching staff in 2023, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2023/9/20/23882831/bears-qb-justin-fields-revisits-coaching-comment-says-put-it-on-me" >he had a staff member gather reporters at his locker hours later to give a statement</a>. Teams also have had a communications executive or other staffer provide background information to clear up perceived inaccuracies.</p><p>The Grade 2 hamstring strain report originated from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Sept. 27. Those are the two foremost news breakers in the league, and it’s common practice for teams to feed them information. Even if the medical update didn’t come from the Bears, it’s highly doubtful they would’ve left it unchecked if it was wrong.</p><p>Moving forward, Williams indicated he hasn’t fully healed, but, “There are certain parameters that allow you to go out there and play.”</p><p>He did not seem concerned about playing twice in five days if he returns Sunday, then has a short turnaround before the Bears host the Patriots on Thursday, saying, “If I’m good to go, I’m good to go.”</p><p>He went through individual drills wearing a black sleeve on his right leg during the part of practice open to the media and looked agile as he worked on pocket footwork and threw on the run. There was no discernible difference in his gait.</p><p>When asked how close he was to his usual athleticism, he said, “I can move, I can run,” and added that he recently clocked one of his fastest sprint times. The injury would not change how he plays, and he’d have no hesitation to run.</p><p>“I’ll take off,” he said.</p><p>He was doing just that when he got hurt. As Williams scrambled toward the end zone late in the 9-3 loss to the Vikings, he felt a pop and fell to the ground untouched. He didn’t know in the moment whether it would be season-ending.</p><p>The thought of being out for the season made him cry as he covered his face with a towel that day, then he got ripped for overdramatizing the injury.</p><p>“I'm always going to show emotion,” Williams said. “This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It's everything to me, so not being able to be out there was frustrating.”</p><p>He added, “My character has been attacked for a while. It's just another motivating factor.”</p><p>Johnson has tried to use his murky quarterback situation to his advantage in Williams’ absence and has been dodgy about naming a starter ahead of games. With Williams working back from an injury and backup Tyson Bagent coming off a disastrous game against the Packers, it’s unclear how those two and third-stringer Case Keenum stack up for Sunday.</p><p>Johnson could clear that up Friday, of course, but that doesn’t seem to be how the Bears operate.</p>

entries.title: Gov. JB Pritzker reports $9.4 million income on 2025 tax returns — and no gambling winnings
entries.summary: <p>It was another strong year for Gov. JB Pritzker in the financial markets, if not at the blackjack table.</p><p>The billionaire governor reported $9.4 million in 2025 income along with first lady MK Pritzker, according to portions of their joint state and federal tax returns released Thursday by Pritzker’s campaign.</p><p>That’s down from the $10.7 million the Pritzkers made the previous year, when the card-playing governor reported <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/illinois-governor/2025/10/15/jb-pritzker-tax-returns-gambling-casino" target="_blank" ><u>gambling winnings of $1.4 million</u></a> that he racked up during a prolific weekend of blackjack in Las Vegas.</p><p>“I was incredibly lucky,” Pritzker said last year of the windfall that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/illinois-governor/2025/10/16/jb-pritzker-gambling-blackjack-win-las-vegas" target="_blank" ><u>went to charity</u></a>.</p><p>No such luck appears on the couple’s latest filing, which lists income of about $1.8 million from taxable interest, $3.6 million from ordinary dividends and $4 million in capital gains.</p><p>The Pritzkers paid about $5.1 million in federal taxes and more than $962,000 to the state of Illinois — both significant overpayments, with differences set to be applied to next year’s tax bills.</p><p>An heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune with a net worth estimated by Forbes at $4.2 billion, Pritzker doesn’t take a salary as governor. He put his investments in a blind trust when he took office in 2019 to avoid potential conflicts of interest.</p><p>Those trusts paid $50.4 million in federal taxes and $8.8 million to the state last year, according to Pritzker’s campaign, which noted the couple made $1.9 million in personal charitable donations.</p><p>Pritzker has pumped a cool $65 million into his reelection campaign as he seeks a rare third term next month. The potential 2028 presidential contender has spent more than $400 million on his campaigns over the years, and given more to other Democrats and liberal causes nationwide.</p><p>Darren Bailey, the Republican southern Illinois farmer trying for a second time <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-illinois-governor-election-november-midterm?5" target="_blank" ><u>to unseat Pritzker</u></a>, reported an adjusted gross income deficit of $99,264 and no taxable income the year before his loss in the 2022 general election.</p><p>In years closely preceding that, Bailey and his wife, Cindy, reported incomes of up to $211,000, while holding thousands of acres of farmland <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2022/9/14/23354150/downstate-republican-darren-bailey-tax-returns-election-governor-farm-subsidy-pritzker" target="_blank" ><u>reasonably valued in the millions of dollars</u></a>.</p><p>Bailey’s campaign didn’t immediately respond to a request for his most recent filings. Neither did the campaign of independent candidate Collin Corbett.</p><p>Bailey posted a meme on the social media platform X suggesting Pritzker's tax return revealed only the tip of the iceberg of the governor's wealth, which is mostly contained in the blind trust.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="zxx" dir="ltr"><a href="https://t.co/N708UpE6bp">pic.twitter.com/N708UpE6bp</a></p>— Darren Bailey (@DarrenBaileyIL) <a href="https://x.com/DarrenBaileyIL/status/2110863685124043011?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 15, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Pritzkers reported an adjusted gross income of $18.5 million in 2021, a little more than half of what they reported the year before the governor took office. Their annual income has otherwise hovered between $2 million to $5 million.</p>

entries.title: 3 who beat, dragged 65-year-old man off Red Line train sought by police
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are looking for three people who beat an elderly man and then dragged him off a CTA Red Line train last Friday.</p><p>The man, 65, was on the train in the 1200 block of North Clark Street, near the Clark/Division Red Line station, when the three of them beat and dragged him off the train before spray-painting his face, police said.</p><p>The suspects were described as a man in his early 20s with a shag hair style and “5718” tattooed on his left knuckles. The other attacker was listed in his early 20s wearing a dark sweater, tan pants and earrings. They were accompanied by a woman in her early 20s wearing a brown coat, black pants and brown boots, police said.</p><p>Anyone with information can contact detectives at 312-745-4447.</p>

entries.title: Cubs parking lot expansion greenlit by Plan Commission but with less spaces
entries.summary: <p>The Cubs were approved to expand its Camry parking lot near Wrigley Field on Thursday — but not for 947 parking spaces, which the team originally proposed.</p><p>The Chicago Plan Commission unanimously approved the Cubs’ lot expansion, at the corner of Racine Avenue and Grace Street, to 800 parking spaces, which is allowed under the parcel’s planned development. </p><p>The new spaces will be added at 1114 W. Grace St., the former House of the Good Shepherd site. The Cubs purchased and then <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/05/28/demolition-lake-view-house-good-shepherd-womens-shelter-cubs-camry-parking-lot-expansion" >demolished the former women’s shelter</a> to make way for its Camry lot expansion. A permit to tear down the two-story building was issued by the city April 20, and demolition began in May.</p><p>The expansion will add 112 spaces to the Camry lot, which currently has parking for 688 vehicles.</p><p>The Cubs announced plans in the spring to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/03/11/chicago-cubs-add-nearly-260-parking-spaces-3-ads-signs-wrigley-field" >expand the lot</a>. The team cited the need for more parking ahead of the 2027 All-Star Game that will be played at Wrigley Field, arguing fans would otherwise park in the neighborhood.</p><p>Lake View neighbors were concerned the proposal would increase traffic. They pressed leaders from the Cubs’ community affairs team to explain why more parking spaces were needed, despite the majority of fans taking public transportation to get to Wrigley.</p><p>About 37% of game attendees drive to Wrigley Field, while 63% use alternate modes of transportation, according to the team. Preliminary numbers from the Cubs’ 2026 season show more than 53% of fans used public transportation to get to Wrigley. That’s “far higher” than most other teams in Chicago and around the country, Mike Lufrano, executive vice president of community and legal affairs for the Cubs, told commissioners Thursday.</p><p>“It is a fact of life that parking is needed for an event arena like Wrigley Field,” Mara Georges, an attorney representing the Cubs, said.</p><p>Existing trees will be retained at the property, and another 33 trees will be planted, in response to neighbor concerns about tree removal. The team is also putting $500,000 toward landscaping and renovations for nearby Kelly Park. The park will not be impacted by the expansion — though it’s undergoing its own renovations, separate from the Cubs’ proposal.</p><p>The additions were made in response to initial neighborhood feedback. Ald. Bennett Lawson (44th) earlier this month opposed the Cubs expanding beyond the 800 parking spaces permitted under the Camry lot’s planned development.</p><p>Lawson said in an Oct. 1 newsletter to neighbors that his decision was based on resident input and his commitment to ensuring that future changes “prioritize community safety, traffic management, and overall quality of life in the neighborhood.”</p><p>Lawson also noted the Wrigley Traffic Management Plan hasn’t been updated in more than a decade. He wants to see changes to that plan implemented before any further parking is added to the Camry lot.</p><p>“While there will always be cars for ballgames, I believe this plan needs to prioritize pedestrian safety, public transit and non-driving options to access the neighborhood,” Lawson wrote.</p><p>The Cubs plan to start work in November and expect it to be complete in May 2027, before the All-Star break.</p><p>“We remain committed to working with the City and our neighbors throughout this process,” the Cubs said in a statement to the Sun-Times.</p><p>The Plan Commission also approved Chicago-based Range Group’s proposal for a five-story, 110-unit apartment building near Fulton Market. The land, at 1133 W. Kinzie St., bordered by Metra tracks to the south, is vacant.</p><p>The $20 million building would include a green roof with an amenity terrace for residents. Rather than being anchored by retail space on the ground level, like many buildings in the neighborhood, Range Group plans for 33 parking spaces and a handful of apartments.</p><p>The building would include studios, one- and two-bedroom apartments. Seventeen of the affordable units, required under the city’s Affordable Requirements Ordinance, would be onsite, while five would be built elsewhere in the 27th ward. Those units will be affordable to renters at or below 60% the area median income, according to the development team.</p><p>Local Ald. Walter R. Burnett (27th) expressed his support for the project, as did community group Neighbors of River West.</p><p>“We need more housing,” Burnett said during the meeting. “This area is becoming more of a bustling residential corridor.”</p>
entries.author: Abby Miller

entries.title: Pappas office receives envelope with 'suspicious' substance, turns out to be baking powder
entries.summary: <p>A suspicious envelope with white powder inside was delivered to Cook County Treasurer Maria Pappas' downtown office Thursday morning. </p><p>The substance inside the envelope, addressed to Pappas, turned out to be baking powder, Pappas told the Sun-Times. Chicago firefighters and police officers responded to the county building at 118 N. Clark St. to investigate the suspicious envelope and had it resolved within 45 minutes, Pappas said. </p><p>"It's frightening," she said. "The whole place went on red alert." </p><p>The envelope was found and opened by an employee in the mailroom on the first floor of her office, Pappas said. He immediately put it inside a plastic bag and brought it upstairs. </p><p>"He's no dummy," Pappas said of the mailroom worker. "He deserves a raise." </p><p>Chicago fire department spokesperson Larry Merritt confirmed firefighters responded to a "level I hazardous materials alarm" at 10:25 a.m. No injuries were reported. </p><p>"One-tenth of 1% of the country are nut jobs causing problems for the 99% of us," Pappas said of the incident. "I can't walk around afraid otherwise I won’t get up in the morning." </p><p>Meanwhile, federal authorities are investigating a series of letters with “suspicious substances” mailed to congressional and election offices nationwide, <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/fbi-postal-service-letters-suspicious-substances-investigation-c90253b9873a27471e63c6f1dcf979e9" target="_blank" >the Associated Press reported Thursday</a>. </p><p>It was not immediately clear whether the envelope sent to Pappas was connected to the other suspicious letters. A spokesperson with the FBI's field office in Chicago confirmed the bureau responded to an incident "in the City Hall vicinity" Thursday, but did not comment directly on the investigation into the envelope found at Pappas' office. </p><p>"The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices," the FBI said in a statement. "Some of the letters contained an unknown substance and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident. We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters." </p><p>"The FBI, they don't take this lightly," Pappas said. "It can happen anywhere."</p>
entries.author: Kaitlin Washburn

entries.title: Bears expect Falcons to try to throw deep, 'can’t be afraid of it'
entries.summary: <p>The Packers threw deep on the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/15/bears-catch-22-michael-penix-left-handed-quarterback-first-time-15-years-dennis-allen-nfl" target="_blank" >Falcons</a> will try to Sunday. So will the Patriots five days later.</p><p>That’s what happens when a team gets exploited the way the Bears did against their rivals. Packers quarterback Jordan Love completed six passes that flew at least 20 yards in the air. They totaled 258 yards, the second-most in the NFL on such throws in 10 years.</p><p>“Teams are not gonna stop throwing the ball up top. …” Bears defensive backs coach Al Harris said Thursday. “Whether it’s the offense, defense or kicking game, once somebody’s successful at whatever that is, then you’ll get it. You’ve gotta expect it. </p><p>"My thing is, you can’t be afraid of it. We’ve got to expect it and be up for a challenge. I think the guys are.”</p><p>We’ll see. The Falcons aren’t as adept at deep shots as the Bears’ rivals — “There’s not too many teams that have deep threats like the Packers do,” cornerback Jaylon Johnson said — but they boast Drake London, who is fourth in the NFL with 488 receiving yards. Their quarterback, Michael Penix, likes to push the limit vertically.</p><p>The question is whether the Bears can stop it. Last week they couldn’t.</p><p>“We didn’t play good. … ” Johnson said. “For us as a unit, as a DB group, we know the game is going to be on us. If we have performance like that, we should expect the game not to go well.”</p><p>The Bears have had two of them — and they’ve both resulted in losses. They gave up 37 points to the Panthers in Week 1 and 31 against the Packers on Sunday. In between, though, they Bears gave up 28 points over three games. The Bears left Lambeau Field on Sunday feeling similar to the way they did flying home from Charlotte.</p><p>“We had a game — first game of the year — we didn't play exceptionally well,” defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said. “We came back and played pretty well in three games, and then we had another poor game. It's kind of the life of the NFL.”</p><p>The Bears can’t ride that roller coaster every week on defense. This week’s nosedive got a little more steep Tuesday, when the NFL announced a two-game performance-enhancing drug suspension for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/13/bears-de-montez-sweat-suspended-2-days-for-drug-violation" >defensive end Montez Sweat.</a> Combine that with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/14/bears-coach-ben-johnson-disappointed-in-de-montez-sweats-suspension-and-now-dayo-odeyingbo-is-out-too" >Dayo Odeyingbo’s quad injury, </a>and the Bears’ defensive backs will suffer from the lack of a pass rush.</p><p>They could get help soon. Nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon must come off the physically-unable-to-perform list next week or be lost for the season. While the Bears figure to ease him back into game action once he’s activated, he’d give Allen another weapon.</p><p>“I think that Kyler can help us win games,” Allen said.</p><p>Otherwise, the Bears need the players they have to show improvement. Johnson has struggled this season; Pro Football Focus has given him the sixth-worst coverage grade out of the 64 cornerbacks who have played at least half their team’s snaps. Malik Muhammad, the fourth-round rookie who has shuffled between the slot and outside cornerback, is 11<sup>th</sup>-worst.</p> <p>Part of the job is “slowing your mind down sometimes,” Johnson said, rather than doing too much.</p><p>“Just being where you’re supposed to be when you’re supposed to be there,” he said.</p><p>Johnson is physical enough to challenge London, who has a tendency to bump defenders at the top of his route.</p><p>“He likes to push. … if they called it every time it wouldn’t make the game fun,” Johnson said.</p><p>Safety and nickel cornerback Cam Lewis said that “just because [London] is physical doesn’t mean we can’t be physical.”</p><p>The Bears know they’ll be tested deep.</p><p>“We’ve got to get that fixed,” Allen said. “That’s got to be better. We’ve been working this week to try and get those things taken care of.”</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: More PPP fraud by Chicago cops found; city's inspector general now says 44 cheated COVID relief programs
entries.summary: <p>Eight more Chicago cops have been caught pocketing pandemic relief money they weren’t entitled to — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/ppp-paycheck-protection-program-covid-relief/2026/07/15/ppp-fraud-pandemic-chicago-police-inspector-general" >pushing the city watchdog’s tally</a> to 44 officers, with more investigations nearing the finish line.</p><p>Inspector General David Glockner said Thursday his office found evidence the eight officers illegally collected more than $191,000 through two federal programs meant to keep businesses afloat during the COVID-19 crisis.</p><p>The latest findings involve money obtained through the Paycheck Protection Program and a federal economic injury disaster assistance program. Both offered a financial lifeline to businesses battered by the pandemic in 2020 and 2021. Hundreds of billions of dollars in fraud have been identified in those same programs.</p><p>Glockner's office recommended firing six of the officers. The other two quit while investigators were still digging.</p><p>The findings add to a growing list of Chicago cops accused of cashing in on pandemic aid.</p><p>In July, Glockner reported closing eight other Chicago police PPP fraud cases. His predecessor, Deborah Witzburg, previously issued reports finding 28 officers bilked the program.</p><p>Now Glockner, who began his four-year term in May, is pushing to clear a backlog of investigations that have been open for more than a year. That includes 67 fraud cases.</p><p>“A substantial portion of the aged fraud cases involve allegations of pandemic assistance fraud and are nearing completion,” Glockner wrote in his quarterly report.</p><p>Many of those remaining cases are expected to involve Chicago police officers.</p><p>The fallout has also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/05/05/chicago-police-cpd-brandi-wright-fraud-ppp-crime" >reached federal court</a>: Two former Chicago cops and a sergeant are awaiting trial on charges of cheating the PPP program.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/ppp-paycheck-protection-program-covid-relief/2026/08/20/chicago-police-cpd-hillard-snelling" >With PPP fraud case looming, son of Chicago’s ex-top cop avoids suspension over chaotic arrest</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/05/05/chicago-police-cpd-brandi-wright-fraud-ppp-crime" >Chicago police sergeant charged with stealing $41K from federal PPP program</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/ppp-paycheck-protection-program-covid-relief/2026/07/15/ppp-fraud-pandemic-chicago-police-inspector-general" >8 more Chicago police officers face firing over PPP loan fraud, City Hall watchdog says</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
